title: Signing: certificates, provisioning profiles and the archive

videos.script: An iPhone runs no code that Apple has not vouched for. {{fee}} So this lesson starts with the price. The Apple Developer Program is ninety-nine dollars a year. Nothing in this course asks you to pay it, and a free account already runs your app on your own phone, for seven days at a time. {{three}} Signing is three pieces. A certificate says who signed. A provisioning profile says what that signer may do, and on which devices. Entitlements say what the app wants. {{chain}} You make a signing request with openssl, and sign it with a certificate authority built for practice. {{missing}} Then you take away the middle link of the chain, and read the error that a missing intermediate gives. {{entitlements}} You check an app's entitlements against what a profile allows. {{xcode}} And you see what Xcode does with all of it: automatic signing, and the archive you hand to App Store Connect. That half needs a Mac and the membership, and it was not run.
